Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:

sentences.text: That on 15.08.2023 at about 05.15 PM., petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-50-EF-7005, in BB Road, wher in his his wife and minor children are the pillion riders, when they came near Honda Show room, Devanahalli town, wherein the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-03-MR- 7636 drove it in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life with high speed and suddenly taken U turn and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident and thereby petitioner sustained simple injuries.
He was shifted to Chiguru hospital, later shifted to Manasa Hospital, wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- for her treatment.
Petitioner stated that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the he was hale and healthy and he is aged about 37 years and he was working in a private company and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent no.2,
who insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and the jurisdictional police have registered the Cr.No.175/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
He pray this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.

3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they have appeared through their counsel and filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioner in toto.

4. Respondents contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and respondent No.1 has contended that the insured has violated the policy conditions and there is no negligence on the part of the insurer and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and produced and marked 11 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 11 and he is fully cross examined.

6. Respondent no.1 examined its official as RW-1, and responded No.2 examined himself as RW.2,
they produced and marked 2 documents which are at Ex.D1 and 2 and they are fully cross examined.
7. I have heard the arguments from both the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

Counsel appearing for respondent no.2 relied on the following authority:
1. The Branch Manager, ICICI Lombard Nibaye Vadde GIC ltd., VS Pooja and others.
Counsel appearing for respondent No.1 has relied on the following authorities:
1. Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - Gopal N vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132614390/
2 MFA No.8009/2002-

8.

On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 15.08.2023 at about 05.15 PM., petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA- 50-EF-7005 on BB Road, near Honda Show room, Devanahalli town, wherein the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-03-MR-7636 drove it in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life with high speed and suddenly taken U turn and dashed to the petitioner motor cycle and caused the accident and thereby petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether respondent No.1 proves that respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?
9.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, 2 IMV report, final report, which are at Ex.P.1 to 8 .
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that respondent No.2 was the driver of offending vehicle and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
The final report which is at Ex.P.8, notice and reply as per section 133 of IMV Act which is at Ex.P.9 and 10.
The entries in the aforesaid documents establish that respondent No.2 is having no valid driving license as on the date of the accident.

Further more final report is filed after investigation and it is Gopal N vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132614390/
3 the prima-facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the cross examination of PW-1 nothing is elicited to disprove the petitioner allegations.
The conduct and approach of respondent No.2 that is not choosing to contest the petition fortifies the petitioner allegation.
Respondents have not challenged the final report filed in the said crime no. and it has reached the finality.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and deserved to be accepted.
12. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate which is at Ex.P.7.
The aforesaid document shows that the petitioner has sustained simple injuries that is abrasion over knees.
Petitioner has not tender document to show the medical expenses for the said injuries.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.10,000/- and petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any heads.
13. Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
14. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, respondent No.2 has admitted that he is having no valid license as on the date of the alleged accident.
The aforesaid fact establishes that respondent No.2 has intentionally violated the policy conditions and liability cannot be fastened on the insurer that is respondent No.1.

The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 argued that respondent No.2 being the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, he cannot seek pay and recovery in view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka that is Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - MFA No.8009/2002- Hon'ble High court of Karnataka order dated 13.01.2006.

entities.text: Venkataramanappa Vs Srinivas and 10 others - MFA No.8009/2002- Hon'ble High court of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has not placed any contrary authority for the same.

With great respect to the aforesaid authorities and by considering the principle laid down therein and by considering the facts and attending circumstances and the conduct of respondent No.2, this Tribunal is of firm conclusion is that the Respondent No.2 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative, issue No.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
15. Issue No.4;

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.10,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.

Draw award accordingly.
